paper.title_en: Evolution of collectivity and emergence of octupole correlations in <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Br</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>77</mn></mmultiscripts></math>
paper.abstract_en: The high-spin states of <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Br</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>77</mn></mmultiscripts></math> have been investigated using the heavy-ion fusion evaporation reaction <math><mrow><mmultiscripts><mi>Cu</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>65</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>(</mo><mmultiscripts><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>19</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi><mi>p</mi><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>Br</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>77</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> at the beam energy of 80 MeV. The level scheme has been upgraded by adding a new band and electric dipole (<math><mrow><mi mathvariant="italic">E</mi><mn mathvariant="italic">1</mn></mrow></math>) transitions between the yrast positive- and negative-parity bands. Lifetimes of excited states have been measured using the Doppler-shift attenuation method to extract the transition strengths and transitional quadrupole moment (<math><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></math>). The deduced transitional quadrupole moment decreases with the increasing spin for both positive- and negative-parity bands, which is supported by the triaxial projected shell model calculations. The enhanced <math><mrow><mi mathvariant="italic">B</mi><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="italic">E</mi><mn mathvariant="italic">1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> strength along with <math><mrow><mi mathvariant="italic">B</mi><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="italic">E</mi><mn mathvariant="italic">1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>/</mo><mi mathvariant="italic">B</mi><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="italic">E</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></math> branching ratio suggests the presence of octupole correlations in <math><mmultiscripts><mi>Br</mi><mprescripts/><none/><mn>77</mn></mmultiscripts></math>.
